steps.body: Leave the house right away. Don't stop to open windows.
No lights, phones or anything that could spark inside the house.
Call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside, away from the house.
Once the utility says it's safe, we'll find and repair the leak.

blocks.h2: Signs Your Gas Line Needs Attention

tiles.body: Utilities add the smell so you notice a leak. Never ignore it.
Near a gas appliance or line, it can mean gas is escaping.
A weak or yellow flame on the stove or water heater can point to a supply problem.
Uncoated brass connectors from decades ago can crack and should be replaced.

bodies: If you suspect a small leak or the utility has shut off service and asked for repairs, we find the exact source. We use electronic gas detectors and soap tests on fittings and pressure-test the system to confirm it's sealed.
Most leaks we find are at fittings, valves and appliance connectors rather than in the pipe itself. Once it's repaired, we test the full system before the gas comes back on.

blocks.h2: Gas Lines in Arlington Heights Homes
blocks.intro: Most homes in Arlington Heights were built between 1940 and 1989, and many still have original gas piping.

items.body: Black iron gas pipe lasts a long time, but threaded joints can loosen and valves can wear over 50 to 80 years.
Old uncoated flexible connectors behind ranges, dryers and water heaters can crack. We replace them with modern coated connectors.
Lines extended for a new range, dryer or grill aren't always done right. We check how they were connected and sized.

blocks.intro: Gas work done right, then tested.

steps.body: Gas line work should be done by a licensed pro. Ours do it every week.
We find the problem and give you a flat price first.
Every repair is tested before the gas goes back on.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: What should I do if I smell gas?
items.preview: Leave, then call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside.
items.answer: Leave the house right away and don't touch any switches. Call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside. Once they say it's safe, call us to repair the leak.

items.q: Can a plumber repair a gas line?
items.preview: Yes. Gas piping should be repaired by a licensed pro.
items.answer: Yes. Gas piping inside your home should be repaired by a licensed pro, and ours are trained for it. The utility handles the meter and the line up to it.

items.q: Who is responsible for the gas line?
items.preview: The utility owns up to the meter. Everything after it is yours.
items.answer: Nicor Gas is responsible for the line up to and including the meter. Piping from the meter to your appliances is the homeowner's responsibility.

items.q: Do old gas connectors need replacing?
items.preview: Uncoated brass ones should be replaced.
items.answer: Yes, if they're old uncoated brass connectors. They can crack over time. Modern coated stainless connectors are safer, and we can swap them during any visit.

items.q: How much does gas line repair cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on the leak and the line. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the leak is, the size of the repair and access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
